comparator.name: English Language and Culture
comparator.sourceNotes: The live Leiden Study Guide confirms a current 180-EC English Language and Culture bachelor and publishes the applicable first and second years in full. Year 1 is a 60-EC compulsory foundation across English language, literature, linguistics and philology. Year 2 contains 45 EC of compulsory language, linguistics, philology, literature and humanities-core study plus 15 EC of restricted literature and philology choices. The displayed 60-EC third year is not applicable to a Fall 2026 entrant: the guide explicitly warns that Year 3 will change significantly from 2027-2028 and separately states that its present compulsory Language Acquisition 5 and 6 modules will be offered for the last time in 2026-2027. Only the supported 120 EC of the entrant's applicable curriculum are retained; the replacement third year is not inferred.

components.name: Year 1 compulsory English-language and cultural foundations
components.note: Compulsory study across spoken and written English, literary studies and historical literature, modern linguistics, Middle and Old English language and literature, and intercultural literary legacies.

components.name: Year 2 compulsory language, linguistics, philology, literature and humanities core
components.note: Compulsory study in rhetorical grammar, written text, English phonology and syntax, history of English, contemporary film and literature, philosophy of science, and humanities in a digital world.

components.name: Year 2 restricted literature and philology choices
components.note: Students select one 5-EC American or British literature course in each semester and one 5-EC medieval or early-modern philology course.

exception.reason: Leiden is revising the third year of English Language and Culture. The current 2026-2027 Study Guide establishes the complete first and second years, but explicitly warns that Year 3 will change significantly from 2027-2028 and that its present compulsory Language Acquisition 5 and 6 courses are being offered for the last time in 2026-2027. A Fall 2026 entrant reaches Year 3 after those legacy courses have ended. Combining the revised 120-EC first-two-year sequence with the outgoing third year would therefore create a pathway the entrant cannot follow; the replacement specialisation, elective and thesis structure cannot be inferred without invention.
exception.curriculumContext: The supported applicable curriculum totals 120 EC. Year 1 is a 60-EC compulsory foundation spanning spoken and written English, literature, linguistics, philology, Old and Middle English, and intercultural literary exchange. Year 2 consists of 45 EC of compulsory advanced language, linguistics, philology, literature and humanities-core study plus 15 EC of restricted choices in American or British literature and medieval or early-modern philology. The official product confirms that the bachelor as a whole is 180 EC, but its displayed 60-EC third year is an outgoing structure and the replacement curriculum for the Fall 2026 cohort is not yet published.
